meta.title: VMA Knowledge Graph
meta.description: Single source of truth for the VMA knowledge graph. Project realm = the live system (routes, components, stores, modules, DB tables, API routes, pipelines, scripts, external services), built from docs/kg/SYSTEM.md and verified against live code. Field realm = the domain (literature, people, methods, gaps). Bridge edges connect project nodes to the field they sit in (uses/instanceOf/runs/implements/feeds/peerOf/inheritsFrom/addresses).
meta.stage: 4 — bridge edges + viewer (project + field + cross-realm bridges)

sources.supabase: maps table, queried 2026-06-04 (corrects the '~20+ Saigon maps' estimate)
sources.field-knowledge-graph.md: docs/field-knowledge-graph.md (field landscape: persons, institutions, projects, methods, gaps)
sources.theory.md: docs/theory.md (VMA theoretical framework: data stack, Lefebvre triad, HITL, body/soul)

corpus.note: Corpus is country-wide, not Saigon-only; largest block is northern Vietnam (Tonkin & Thanh Hóa).

schema.node: { id, label, realm, kind, detail, status, source:[{ref,date}], deck:[] }
schema.deck: Tags for deck derivation (stage 5): 'seminar' | 'ewv'. Empty until populated.
schema.realms: project (the live system) | field (the domain: literature, people, methods, gaps)

meta.statusNote: 'gap' = an identified absence: research-contribution gaps (kind:gap) and canonical works missing from the library (kind:work).

nodes.label: /login

nodes.label: /contribute
nodes.detail: Hub page explaining the ways to help; content adapts to user role.

nodes.label: /explore
nodes.detail: Canonical map viewer. Modern basemap + historical overlays; one-time location chooser, first-visit guided tour, GPS coverage lookup, story playback. Honors ?map=, ?story= and the URL hash.

nodes.label: /studio
nodes.detail: Canonical drawing/annotation surface (StudioMode). Points, lines, polygons; drives an animation/keyframe timeline for animated story scenes.

nodes.label: /create
nodes.detail: Build stories and adventures (guided point-to-point tours) — CreateMode.

nodes.label: /trip/[id]
nodes.detail: Tourist-grade mobile story player: GPS walks the user stop-to-stop, no account needed. Built for QR-code scanning in the field.

nodes.label: /image
nodes.detail: Inspector for a single IIIF image in pixel coordinates.

nodes.label: /contribute/georef
nodes.detail: Georeference a map via the Allmaps editor — pin matching points between the old map and the real world.

nodes.label: /contribute/trace
nodes.detail: Trace building footprints (polygons) and roads/rivers (lines) on a fixed map image. Persists to footprint_submissions.

nodes.label: /contribute/review
nodes.detail: HITL review of MapSAM2 'submitted'/'needs_review' building polygons — approve/reject + mark seg reviewed.

nodes.label: /contribute/digitalize
nodes.detail: Two-phase HITL: Triage (neatline rect + tile priority grid) → OCR Review (correct text/category/position). Owns the OCR review flow.

nodes.label: /admin/bulk
nodes.detail: Admin-only: batch-create draft maps rows; outputs tile commands.

nodes.label: /admin/scout
nodes.detail: Admin-only: reviewable grid of scout_candidates auto-discovered from Gallica/Humazur/Rumsey/LoC.

nodes.label: /view → /explore
nodes.detail: 301 redirect to /explore (the viewer was folded into Explore). Query strings preserved.

nodes.label: /annotate → /studio
nodes.detail: 301 redirect to /studio (drawing moved to Studio). Query strings preserved. NOTE: older docs claim /studio → /annotate — that is reversed and wrong.

nodes.label: /contribute/label → /contribute/digitalize
nodes.detail: 301 redirect to /contribute/digitalize (labeling absorbed into Digitalize). Query strings preserved.

nodes.label: MapShell
nodes.detail: Owns the single OpenLayers Map; entry point for all geo-map pages. Mounts basemap tile layers, exposes everything via Svelte context (getShellContext). Children never create a second OL map.

nodes.label: ImageShell
nodes.detail: IIIF-canvas counterpart to MapShell for pixel-coordinate work. Static image extent, getImageShellStore(). Used by /contribute/digitalize, /contribute/trace, /contribute/review — does NOT use MapShell or global stores.

nodes.label: LayerRenderer
nodes.detail: The single component that renders ALL map layers — base (modern tile OR historical warped) and overlays — by subscribing to layersStore. Owns basemap visibility. Replaces the removed HistoricalOverlay/HistoricalBaseLayer/StackedOverlay trio.

nodes.label: DualMapPane
nodes.detail: Side-by-side view mode. Independently renders overlays[1] in the right pane.

nodes.label: MapWorkspace
nodes.detail: Shared map chrome (panels, mobile drawers) wrapped around the map by both /explore and /trip.

nodes.label: MapModeOverlays
nodes.detail: Shared shell piece for mode-specific map overlay UI.

nodes.label: DrawTool
nodes.detail: Shared OL drawing tool used by the Studio annotation surface.

nodes.label: GpsTracker
nodes.detail: Shared GPS/geolocation tracker (used by /explore coverage lookup and /trip story player).

nodes.label: HistoricalOverlay (removed)
nodes.detail: REMOVED. Was a headless overlay reacting to activeAllmapsId + layerStore. Replaced by LayerRenderer + layersStore. Kept as a tombstone node because stale docs (knowledge-graph.html) still reference it.

nodes.label: CreateMode
nodes.detail: Root component for /create (story/adventure builder).

nodes.label: StudioMode
nodes.detail: Root component for /studio drawing surface. Carries an animation/ keyframe system (playback + timelineStore). Replaces the removed AnnotateMode.

nodes.label: ReviewMode
nodes.detail: Root component for /contribute/review footprint HITL.

nodes.label: TraceTool
nodes.detail: OL Draw + Select + Modify for polygon (footprints) / line (roads, waterways) tracing on /contribute/trace.

nodes.label: TraceSidebar
nodes.detail: Shapes table with category/type filtering for /contribute/trace.

nodes.label: TriageTool
nodes.detail: Neatline rect + tile priority grid (digitalize Triage phase). Click cycles tile: normal → low-res → skip → normal.

nodes.label: TriageSidebar
nodes.detail: Tile params + Run OCR controls for digitalize Triage.

nodes.label: OcrBboxTool
nodes.detail: Renders + edits ocr_extractions bboxes; drawMode for manual bboxes (POSTs model:'manual'). Reused verbatim by digitalize OCR Review.

nodes.label: OcrSidebar
nodes.detail: Filterable table with inline text/category edit + auto-save on blur.

nodes.label: ReviewCanvas
nodes.detail: Canvas for SAM2 footprint review on ImageShell.

nodes.label: ReviewSidebar
nodes.detail: Approve/reject + 'Mark seg reviewed' (PATCHes pipeline → seg_reviewed).

nodes.label: MapEditModal
nodes.detail: Multi-tab admin modal: Metadata · Hosting · Pipeline · GCPs. Inline in /catalog for admin/mod.

nodes.label: FacetRail
nodes.detail: Multi-select facet chips with 'all-but-this-dimension' tallies for unified search.

nodes.label: SearchResultCard
nodes.detail: Result card for unified maps + scout search.

nodes.label: bboxHandles.ts
nodes.detail: Centralised handle features + IIIF y-flip for all bbox-editing tools.

nodes.label: layersStore
nodes.detail: Single source of truth for what the map renders: { base: LayerRef, overlays: OverlayLayer[] }. base = basemap key OR historical map; overlays top-of-stack-first, each with own opacity/visible/id (max 10). Persists to localStorage (vma-layers-v1).

nodes.label: mapStore
nodes.detail: { lng, lat, zoom, rotation, activeMapId, activeAllmapsId }. Default Saigon (106.70098, 10.77653) zoom 14. activeMapId is now a one-way mirror of layersStore.overlays[0] (kept for legacy callers).

nodes.label: layerStore (legacy)
nodes.detail: { basemap, overlayOpacity, overlayVisible, viewMode, sideRatio, lensRadius }. Only viewMode/sideRatio/lensRadius still matter; basemap/opacity/visible are legacy — layersStore owns rendering now.

nodes.label: urlStore
nodes.detail: Bidirectional URL hash ↔ stores sync. Hash: #@lat,lng,zoomz,rotationr&map=id&base=key.

nodes.label: annotationState
nodes.detail: Annotation list + selection + undo/redo history (GeoJSON snapshots, 100-entry limit). Used by StudioMode.

nodes.label: lib/maps/
nodes.detail: Data layer for the maps table; canonical home for shared types. types, service, iiifManifest, adminApi.

nodes.label: lib/iiif/
nodes.detail: buildAnnotation, fetchIiifInfoWithRetry, fetchIIIFImageInfo.

nodes.label: lib/supabase/
nodes.detail: Browser + SSR clients, auth context, data-layer modules (annotations, stories, labels, georef). labels.ts has SAM2 review entry points.

nodes.label: contribute/shared/
nodes.detail: Shared contribute UI: ToolPanelHeader, EmptyPanel, SidebarToggleButton, bboxHandles (y-flip).

nodes.label: maps
nodes.detail: Map catalogue. id (uuid), allmaps_id (16-char hex), annotation_url (mig 047 override), iiif_image, source_type, holding_institution, collection, map_type, bbox, status (draft/public/featured), thumbnail, full DC fields. 101 rows as of 2026-06-04 (37 public / 64 draft; 39 georef_done) — country-wide, not Saigon-only.

nodes.label: map_iiif_sources
nodes.detail: Multiple IIIF sources per map. Partial unique index = one primary. Trigger syncs primary to maps.iiif_image.

nodes.label: scout_candidates
nodes.detail: External discoveries (mig 045). (source, external_id) unique. status: pending → approved/rejected → ingested; map_id set on ingest.

nodes.label: label_tasks
nodes.detail: Per-map point-labeling tasks. map_id → maps.id (join through maps; no allmaps_id).

nodes.label: label_pins
nodes.detail: Point annotations, pixel coords. task_id → label_tasks.id.

nodes.label: footprint_submissions
nodes.detail: Polygon/line traces (human + MapSAM2). map_id → maps.id. Status: needs_review → submitted/rejected.

nodes.label: annotation_sets
nodes.detail: User-drawn GeoJSON. map_id nullable, user_id → auth.users.

nodes.label: ocr_extractions
nodes.detail: OCR bbox results. (map_id, run_id, tile_x, tile_y, text) unique; global_* full-image px; status ∈ pending/validated/rejected.

nodes.label: map_pipeline_status
nodes.detail: Per-map pipeline state. map_id PK, stage (8-value enum: idle → ocr_queued → ocr_done → reviewed → seg_queued → seg_done → seg_reviewed → exported), ocr_run_id, seg_run_id, timestamps. Auto-updated by OCR --db and SAM2 --write-supabase.

nodes.label: hunts
nodes.detail: Stories/tours (legacy table name; Story types alias these).

nodes.label: hunt_stops
nodes.detail: Story waypoints (legacy table name).

nodes.label: .../lookup-allmaps-id

nodes.label: .../fetch-iiif-metadata
nodes.detail: POST { manifestUrl } → parsed IIIF metadata + Allmaps probe.

nodes.label: /api/admin/maps/sync-georef
nodes.detail: Sync georeference state for maps (new since last doc sweep). Lives at maps/sync-georef, not under [id].

nodes.label: /api/admin/upload-image

nodes.label: bulk_upload_local.sh

nodes.label: scout_humazur.mjs

nodes.label: apply_metadata_backfill.mjs

nodes.label: Internet Archive
nodes.detail: S3 upload for original scans (IA_S3_*).

nodes.label: Gallica (BnF) SRU
nodes.detail: BnF digital library; scout source via SRU.

nodes.label: Humazur (Omeka S)
nodes.detail: Université Côte d'Azur archive; scout source via Omeka S API.

nodes.label: David Rumsey Luna
nodes.detail: David Rumsey Map Collection; scout source via Luna.

nodes.label: Library of Congress
nodes.detail: LoC JSON API; scout source.

nodes.label: Gemini Flash API
nodes.detail: Google Gemini Flash — OCR text extraction model.

nodes.label: OpenLayers
nodes.detail: Primary map engine (MapShell + ImageShell). @allmaps/openlayers warps historical tiles.

nodes.label: MapLibre GL
nodes.detail: Lightweight embed-only map (src/lib/Map.svelte) via @allmaps/maplibre.

nodes.label: Bert Spaan
nodes.detail: Built Allmaps — IIIF-native client-side WebGL warping; co-authored the IIIF Georeference Extension. The field’s current georef standard, which VMA runs on.

nodes.label: Jules Schoonman
nodes.detail: TU Delft Library; co-founder + institutional face of Allmaps. Bridges the library world to the technical pipeline.

nodes.label: Manuel Claeys Bouuaert
nodes.detail: Allmaps core team; the geometric/transformation math + benchmark tooling.

nodes.label: Ian Spangler
nodes.detail: Leventhal Map Center (Boston PL). Ran Allmaps at scale for Atlascope (145+ Boston atlases) — the production exemplar.

nodes.label: Tim Waters
nodes.detail: Built MapWarper (Ruby/PostGIS/GDAL) — the pre-Allmaps workhorse, still core to the Wikimedia/Wikidata map ecosystem.

nodes.label: Martijn Meijers
nodes.detail: TU Delft; semi-automatic georeferencing of rectangular map series — directly relevant to VMA’s uniform L7014 grid.

nodes.label: Camille Morlighem
nodes.detail: TU Delft (MSc 2021). Built histo3d: historical map → OBIA → polygonize → LoD2 CityJSON. >84% plots, >99% valid geometry — but only under strict symbology (the central risk).

nodes.label: Hugo Ledoux
nodes.detail: TU Delft 3D Geoinformation; creator of CityJSON (cjio, val3dity, City4CFD). Co-supervised Morlighem. VMA’s strongest technical-PhD supervisor target.

nodes.label: Anna Labetski
nodes.detail: TU Delft 3D Geoinformation; co-supervised Morlighem; 3D urban modelling + historical reconstruction.

nodes.label: Lorenz Hurni
nodes.detail: Head of ETH IKG; founded ETH’s historical-map vectorization + generative-cartography research; supervises Wu and Chen.

nodes.label: Sidi Wu
nodes.detail: ETH IKG. Cross-attention spatio-temporal transformer for segmentation across map editions; unsupervised historical-map registration via deformation nets.

nodes.label: Yizi Chen
nodes.detail: ETH IKG / LRDE-EPITA (two people share the name). Lead author of the 2024 PLoS ONE vectorization benchmark — the field’s first systematic method comparison.

nodes.label: Konrad Schindler
nodes.detail: ETH Zurich Photogrammetry; co-supervises Wu/Chen; the CV-on-historical-imagery bridge.

nodes.label: Julien Perret
nodes.detail: IGN France; PI on SODUCO — deep-learning pipelines for historical Paris maps. SODUCO is VMA’s closest methodological peer.

nodes.label: Yao-Yi Chiang
nodes.detail: USC/UMN; long line of work using historical maps as scientific data; contributor to Machines Reading Maps. (Library: “using historical maps in scientific…”)

nodes.label: Mauricio Giraldo Arteaga
nodes.detail: NYPL Labs; built Building Inspector + Map Vectorizer — the canonical HITL (auto + crowd) precedent VMA’s loop inherits.

nodes.label: Isabella Di Lenardo
nodes.detail: EPFL DH Lab; bridges Venice Time Machine + SODUCO; spatial urban history + archival document processing.

nodes.label: Rémi Petitpierre
nodes.detail: EPFL DH Lab; automatic feature extraction from historical maps; effective annotation for cadastral-map vectorization (in library).

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/04-vma-pipeline/Petitpierre 2023 Effective annotation for the automatic vectorization of cadastral maps.pdf

nodes.label: Leon van Wissen
nodes.detail: Univ. Amsterdam / KNAW; geotemporal KG for historical cities (Amsterdam Time Machine, GLOBALISE). VMA’s most direct KG peer.

nodes.label: Katherine McDonough
nodes.detail: Lancaster + Alan Turing Institute; PI of Machines Reading Maps; built MapReader (AHA Roy Rosenzweig Prize 2023). The clearest bridge-figure career model.

nodes.label: Frédéric Kaplan
nodes.detail: EPFL; founded Venice Time Machine → Time Machine Europe. Shows one city-history project becoming massive institutional infrastructure — VMA’s aspirational scaling model.

nodes.label: Christophe Verbruggen
nodes.detail: Ghent University; DH; Artemis (Scheldt-valley environmental history via historical maps).

nodes.label: Anne Kelly Knowles
nodes.detail: Univ. Maine; defined HGIS in the English-speaking world (Past Time Past Place; Placing History). Model of the geographer-historian who learned GIS as method.

nodes.label: Ian Gregory
nodes.detail: Lancaster; coined “spatial humanities”; geographical text analysis on historical corpora (incl. colonial Mexico). Closest method + career fit for VMA’s KG/text pipeline.

nodes.label: Peter Bol
nodes.detail: Harvard (emeritus); built CHGIS — the infrastructure template for HGIS. A Song historian who learned spatial analysis mid-career: the closest career analogy to VMA’s founder.

nodes.label: Humphrey Southall
nodes.detail: Univ. Portsmouth; built Great Britain Historical GIS / A Vision of Britain Through Time — the scalability-engineering model for queryable historical boundaries.

nodes.label: Ruth Mostern
nodes.detail: Univ. Pittsburgh (ISHI); World Historical Gazetteer → The Yellow River (Levenson Prize). The full infrastructure→prize-winning-scholarship arc VMA aspires to.

nodes.label: Richard White
nodes.detail: Stanford (emeritus); founded the Spatial History Lab; “What is Spatial History?” — spatial visualization as argument, not illustration.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/02-hgis-methodology/what is spatial history pub 020110 richard white.pdf

nodes.label: Elijah Meeks
nodes.detail: Built ORBIS (Roman-world geospatial network) at Stanford; co-edited Toward Spatial Humanities. Shows tool-builders can produce real scholarship (and that the skill has industry value).

nodes.label: M.R.G. Conzen
nodes.detail: German émigré geographer (Newcastle); founded the Conzenian school — street systems / plot patterns / building fabric → “plan units.” The analytical vocabulary for historical urban morphology.

nodes.label: J.W.R. Whitehand
nodes.detail: Birmingham (Urban Morphology Research Group); disseminated the Conzenian tradition; founded the journal Urban Morphology.

nodes.label: Saverio Muratori
nodes.detail: Founded the Italian school of “operational history” (1940s–60s); the city read through building-type evolution.

nodes.label: Gianfranco Caniggia
nodes.detail: Extended Muratori into “procedural typology” — conceptual base for Morlighem’s procedural LoD2 modelling.

nodes.label: Gwendolyn Wright
nodes.detail: Columbia GSAPP; The Politics of Design in French Colonial Urbanism (1991) — the founding text; colonies as planning laboratories. Required reading for colonial Saigon.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/01-phd-priority/Wright - Politics of Design in French Colonial Urbanism (1991).pdf

nodes.label: Eric T. Jennings
nodes.detail: Univ. Toronto; most prolific current scholar of French Indochina urban history (Imperial Heights: Dalat); co-translated Brocheux & Hémery.

nodes.label: Haydon Cherry
nodes.detail: Northwestern; Down and Out in Saigon (2019) — the most-cited recent social history of colonial Saigon, from the underclass. Deep archival, no spatial methods.

nodes.label: Nicola Cooper
nodes.detail: Univ. Bristol; foundational article on urban planning + architecture in colonial Indochina; France in Indochina.

nodes.label: Ambe J. Njoh
nodes.detail: Univ. South Florida; French Urbanism in Foreign Lands; Saigon + Dakar street naming. Publishes in Planning Perspectives — the right venue for VMA’s planning-framed paper.

nodes.label: Brocheux & Hémery
nodes.detail: CNRS/Paris; Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization 1858–1954 — the standard comprehensive synthesis.

nodes.label: Paul Rabinow
nodes.detail: French Modern (1989) — norms + forms of the social environment; the genealogy of French planning rationality that produced colonial urbanism.

nodes.label: Erik Harms
nodes.detail: Yale anthropologist; Saigon’s Edge (2011) + Luxury and Rubble (2016) — ethnography of HCMC’s expanding edges and eviction. VMA’s contemporary-Saigon ethnographic anchor.

nodes.label: Huỳnh Thế Du
nodes.detail: Fulbright/policy economist; Quy hoạch Sài Gòn–TPHCM 1858–2024; “Misuse of Urban Planning in HCMC.” A VMA letter writer — positions the work as policy-grounded.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/03-vietnam-indochina/Huynh The Du - Quy hoach Sai Gon - TPHCM 1858-2024 (2024).pdf

nodes.label: Danielle Labbé
nodes.detail: Univ. Montreal; Land Politics and Livelihoods on the Margins of Hanoi — peri-urban land conversion under market socialism.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/01-phd-priority/Labbe - Land Politics and Livelihoods on the Margins of Hanoi (2014).pdf

nodes.label: Jonathan Pincus
nodes.detail: Development economist (Fulbright); a VMA letter writer. With Huỳnh Thế Du, frames the application as a policy-grounded Vietnam specialist.

nodes.label: Henri Lefebvre
nodes.detail: The Production of Space (1974) + Le Droit à la ville (1968). The triad (conçu/perçu/vécu) is VMA’s organizing frame for the data stack.

nodes.label: David Harvey
nodes.detail: Social Justice and the City; The Right to the City — urbanization as capital accumulation; the political-economy lens on who the city is built for.

nodes.label: James C. Scott
nodes.detail: Seeing Like a State (1998) — legibility, high-modernist planning, the map/cadastre as instruments of state simplification. Core critique for reading colonial surveys.

nodes.label: J.B. Harley
nodes.detail: “Deconstructing the Map” (1989) — maps as rhetoric + power, never neutral. The critical-cartography foundation for treating colonial maps as arguments.

nodes.label: Jane Jacobs
nodes.detail: The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961) — street-level urban vitality; the anti-high-modernist counterweight.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/07-general-theory/Jacobs - The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961).pdf

nodes.label: Kevin Lynch
nodes.detail: The Image of the City (1960) — legibility, mental maps (paths/edges/districts/nodes/landmarks). Vocabulary for the perceived-space layer.

nodes.label: Lewis Mumford
nodes.detail: The City in History (1961) — the long-durée of urban form + power; the deep-time framing.

nodes.label: Michel Foucault
nodes.detail: “Of Other Spaces / Heterotopias” (1984) — space as ordered by power; the colonial city as a disciplinary spatial order.

nodes.label: Edward Soja
nodes.detail: Postmodern Geographies (1989) — the “spatial turn”; reasserting space as constitutive of social theory.

nodes.label: Ananya Roy
nodes.detail: “Slumdog Cities: Rethinking Subaltern Urbanism” — theorizing the Global-South city on its own terms; informality as a mode of urbanization.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/07-general-theory/Roy - Slumdog Cities Rethinking Subaltern Urbanism IJURR (2011).pdf

nodes.label: AbdouMaliq Simone
nodes.detail: “People as Infrastructure” (Johannesburg, 2004) — social practice as urban infrastructure; the lens for the lived/memory layer.

nodes.label: Peter Hall
nodes.detail: Cities of Tomorrow / Urban Future 21 — the standard history of 20th-c planning thought; situates colonial + modernist planning in the global story.

nodes.label: Felicity Scott
nodes.detail: Columbia GSAPP (Architecture PhD). Active project on Cambodia/Indochina post-colonial modernism; teaches “Documenting the Colonial Archive.” Closest intellectual match to VMA’s EFEO/BnF + spatial work.

nodes.label: Hiba Bou Akar
nodes.detail: Columbia GSAPP (Urban Planning PhD); For the War Yet to Come (Beirut). Decolonial/post-conflict planning; directs the Post-Conflict Cities Lab; takes students. Her theory, VMA’s city.

nodes.label: Laura Kurgan
nodes.detail: Columbia GSAPP; directs the Center for Spatial Research; Close Up at a Distance (2013). The spatial-methods co-advisor (with Bou Akar).

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/02-hgis-methodology/Close Up at a Distance- Mapping, Technology, and Politics -- Kurgan, Laura -- Princeton University Press, Brooklyn, NY, 2013 -- Brooklyn, NY - Zone -- 9781935408284 -- c4878ed89cfd3146ab6b34b44f66c096 -- Anna’s Archive.pdf

nodes.label: Weiping Wu
nodes.detail: Columbia GSAPP; directs the MS Urban Planning program; East/SE-Asian urban expertise. Likely too administratively occupied for primary supervision — verify.

nodes.label: Bish Sanyal
nodes.detail: MIT DUSP; history of planning ideas, planning in newly industrializing nations, Global-South housing. The closest DUSP comes to a colonial/postcolonial planning historian.

nodes.label: Lawrence Vale
nodes.detail: MIT DUSP; urban design + capital-city planning; decolonization + spatial politics of monuments. Useful committee member (Saigon as “Paris of the East”).

nodes.label: Diane Davis
nodes.detail: Harvard GSD; Latin America, post-conflict cities, urban governance — but sociological/political-science methods, not spatial. Not a strong supervisor match.

nodes.label: Rahul Mehrotra
nodes.detail: Harvard GSD; Asian urbanism, informal/scarcity urbanism. Better as committee/secondary advisor than primary.

nodes.label: TU Delft 3D Geoinformation
nodes.detail: Ledoux + Labetski; CityJSON home; histo3d’s lab; Allmaps Library co-founder (Schoonman). VMA’s strongest technical-PhD target — the georef pipeline is the input histo3d needs.

nodes.label: ETH IKG
nodes.detail: Institute of Cartography & Geoinformation (Hurni, Wu, Chen, Schindler). State-of-the-art map-vectorization + cross-edition change detection. Swiss-style focus → Indochina is genuinely new to them.

nodes.label: EPFL Digital Humanities Lab
nodes.detail: Kaplan, Di Lenardo, Petitpierre. Venice Time Machine + historical-document digitization at scale; SODUCO ties.

nodes.label: Alan Turing Institute
nodes.detail: UK national ML+humanities institute; Living with Machines / Machines Reading Maps / MapReader. The DH-postdoc bridge model.

nodes.label: Leventhal Map & Education Center (Boston PL)
nodes.detail: Allmaps-at-scale via Atlascope (Spangler). The production-deployment exemplar.

nodes.label: KNAW Humanities Cluster
nodes.detail: Dutch national humanities cluster; HisGIS (Stapel), Amsterdam Time Machine / GLOBALISE (van Wissen). KG + cadastral-vectorization peer.

nodes.label: IGN / ENSG France
nodes.detail: French national mapping agency; SODUCO co-lead (Perret). Series-georef + historical-map DL.

nodes.label: EPITA / LRDE (Paris)
nodes.detail: Image-processing lab; SODUCO partner; home of the vectorization benchmark (Y. Chen, LRDE).

nodes.label: Columbia GSAPP
nodes.detail: Architecture + Urban Planning PhDs. Wright’s legacy of colonial-urbanism scholarship; current targets Scott, Bou Akar, Kurgan. A top VMA PhD destination.

nodes.label: MIT DUSP
nodes.detail: Dept. of Urban Studies & Planning; Sanyal, Vale. Planning history + Global-South development; policy-grounded fit.

nodes.label: Harvard GSD
nodes.detail: Graduate School of Design; Davis, Mehrotra. Strong design/theory; weaker on historical spatial methods.

nodes.label: Lancaster University (DH / History)
nodes.detail: Gregory + McDonough; HGIS, spatial humanities, geographical text analysis. Home of the Spatial Humanities conference. Best fit for VMA’s Phase-2 humanities pivot.

nodes.label: Harvard CGA
nodes.detail: Center for Geographic Analysis; CHGIS + geospatial infrastructure (Bol legacy).

nodes.label: Stanford CESTA
nodes.detail: Center for Spatial & Textual Analysis; Spatial History Lab, ORBIS (White/Meeks legacy).

nodes.label: Univ. Pittsburgh ISHI
nodes.detail: Institute for Spatial History Innovation (Mostern); World Historical Gazetteer — global linked-places HGIS infrastructure.

nodes.label: BnF / Gallica
nodes.detail: 10M+ items; France–Vietnam Digital Library; IIIF-native (Gallica manifests load straight into Allmaps). VMA’s primary source archive.

nodes.label: EFEO
nodes.detail: École française d’Extrême-Orient (founded 1898, Saigon); Indochina heritage inventory; active Hanoi + HCMC centers. Essential French partner for archives + ANR co-application.

nodes.label: Perry-Castañeda Library (UT Austin)
nodes.detail: Holds US Army L7014 1:50,000 Vietnam topos as GeoPDF — VMA’s pipeline source for the L7014 series.

nodes.label: Texas Tech Vietnam Center
nodes.detail: 1,500+ Vietnam maps (mostly AMS), incl. L7014 — the JPEG source VMA streams to Internet Archive.

nodes.label: David Rumsey Map Collection
nodes.detail: 150k+ maps, 56k+ georeferenced via a proprietary Georeferencer. Not IIIF-native; a separate ecosystem. One of VMA’s catalogue sources.

nodes.label: Fulbright University Vietnam
nodes.detail: VMA founder’s institution; Digitizing Việt Nam (Luce-funded, textual). Letter-writer base (Huỳnh Thế Du, Pincus).

nodes.label: NYPL Labs
nodes.detail: Built Building Inspector + Map Vectorizer (Giraldo) — the canonical HITL map-vectorization program.

nodes.label: Meta AI
nodes.detail: Built RapiD — AI-proposed road features confirmed by OSM volunteers; the industrial-scale HITL model VMA’s loop mirrors.

nodes.label: HOT (Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team)
nodes.detail: Tasking Manager tile decomposition + Missing Maps. The volunteer task-decomposition model for VMA’s footprint tracing; OSM-Vietnam outreach channel.

nodes.label: Zooniverse
nodes.detail: People-powered research platform (1.6M+ volunteers); Project Builder for custom workflows. A possible HITL platform reference.

nodes.label: Cornell SEAP
nodes.detail: Southeast Asia Program (founded 1950); unmatched Vietnam-studies prestige + archive. No spatial-methods group — better as affiliate than primary program.

nodes.label: SOAS London
nodes.detail: Strong SE-Asian studies + colonial-archive collections; key UK area-studies relationship.

nodes.label: National Library of Scotland
nodes.detail: 60k Ordnance Survey maps processed by MapReader — the at-scale MRM application reference.

nodes.label: Yale-NUS / SE Asia historical maps
nodes.detail: 1,400+ pre-1900 digitized maps (NLB Singapore, Beinecke, Bodleian, Leiden); Dutch-colonial-Indonesia emphasis.

nodes.label: KITLV Leiden
nodes.detail: Royal Institute for Linguistics, Land & Ethnology; SE-Asia maps, Dutch-colonial focus.

nodes.label: Allmaps
nodes.detail: The field’s IIIF-native georef standard; W3C Georeference Annotations; partners TU Delft, Leventhal, LoC, AGSL; funded by Pica. VMA is built on it.

nodes.label: MapWarper
nodes.detail: Open-source Ruby/PostGIS/GDAL georectifier (Waters) — the pre-Allmaps workhorse, still core to Wikimedia/Wikidata.

nodes.label: Atlascope
nodes.detail: Leventhal/BPL — 145+ Massachusetts urban atlases georeferenced + served as overlays. Full-Allmaps-pipeline-at-scale exemplar.

nodes.label: HisGIS
nodes.detail: KNAW/Fryske Akademy — vectorizes 17k Dutch cadastral maps (3M+ parcels); adopted Allmaps for the georef phase.

nodes.label: histo3d
nodes.detail: Morlighem/TU Delft — raster → OBIA → polygonize → height inference → Blender BCGA → LoD2 CityJSON. Open (CC-BY); Delft + Brussels. The 3D pipeline VMA’s georef feeds.

nodes.label: SODUCO
nodes.detail: ANR, Paris 1789–1950 — reference atlases + 113 digitized trade directories → urban-history KG; all open science. VMA’s closest methodological peer (same loop, different city).

nodes.label: Vectorization Benchmark (Chen 2024)
nodes.detail: First systematic comparison of historical-map vectorization methods (PLoS ONE). Finding: ViT/PVT for large objects, U-Net for small. Code + data open.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/04-vma-pipeline/Chen et al (2024) Automatic vectorization of historical maps A benchmark.pdf

nodes.label: MapReader / Machines Reading Maps
nodes.detail: McDonough/Turing+USC+UMN — open Python CV library; 60k OS maps → 1.76M building + 487k railway records. AHA Roy Rosenzweig Prize 2023.

nodes.label: Venice Time Machine
nodes.detail: EPFL + Ca’ Foscari (since 2012) — 80km of archives, IIIF server + HTR pipelines. Seed of Time Machine Europe.

nodes.label: Time Machine Europe
nodes.detail: EU H2020 flagship, 200+ institutions; 20+ Local Time Machines; goal: a 4D simulator of European history. The institutional scaling VMA models.

nodes.label: UrbanHistory4D
nodes.detail: TU Dresden + Würzburg — 4D browser of 3,600 Dresden historical photos in a 3D city model + AR. A Local Time Machine instance.

nodes.label: NYPL Building Inspector + Map Vectorizer
nodes.detail: Auto-detect building polygons from fire-insurance atlases + crowd verification (170k polygons in 24h). VMA’s direct HITL precedent.

nodes.label: RapiD (Meta)
nodes.detail: AI predicts roads from imagery → OSM volunteers confirm/adjust; 300k+ miles of Thailand roads in 18 months. The industrial HITL model.

nodes.label: OpenHistoricalMap
nodes.detail: OSM fork with a time dimension (dated features, not deletions); temporal vector tiles + iD fork. A data destination for VMA’s vectorized footprints.

nodes.label: CHGIS
nodes.detail: China Historical GIS (Bol, Harvard + Fudan) — place names + admin units 222 BCE–1911 CE. The infrastructure template for every later large-scale HGIS.

nodes.label: GB Historical GIS
nodes.detail: Southall/Portsmouth — all censuses + admin geographies 1801–present (A Vision of Britain Through Time). The scalability-engineering model.

nodes.label: World Historical Gazetteer
nodes.detail: Mostern/ISHI — global infrastructure linking historical place-name datasets (uses Linked Places). The standard VMA’s KG should align to.

nodes.label: ORBIS
nodes.detail: Stanford (Meeks + Scheidel) — geospatial network model of the Roman world. Canonical humanist + tool-builder collaboration that produced real scholarship.

nodes.label: Pelagios / Linked Places
nodes.detail: Open standard + infrastructure for linking historical place datasets across projects. VMA’s KG should be Linked-Places-compatible.

nodes.label: GLOBALISE / Necessary Reunions
nodes.detail: KNAW — integrates VOC archives with historical maps of Kerala + SE Asia via KG linking. Textual + cartographic fusion peer.

nodes.label: Vienna History Wiki
nodes.detail: Large collaborative KG of Vienna’s history, linked to Wikidata. The closest published comparison for VMA’s KG layer.

nodes.label: MapSAM2 (Xia 2025)
nodes.detail: Fine-tuned SAM2 for historical-map segmentation; 10-shot viable. VMA runs a LoRA fork (work/MapSAM2) for footprint inference.

nodes.label: OBIA vectorization
nodes.detail: Object-Based Image Analysis: segment a raster into homogeneous regions → classify by symbology → polygonize. Morlighem/histo3d + ETH IKG core method. Fragile to inconsistent symbology.

nodes.label: GCP grid propagation
nodes.detail: Fit an affine model to a seed sheet’s GCPs, project neatline corners to WGS84, then extrapolate adjacent sheets via the series’ Δlon/Δlat. Exploits uniform military-grid geometry — no feature matching. VMA’s novel L7014 method.

nodes.label: Helmert datum correction
nodes.detail: 3-parameter geocentric shift Indian 1960 (Everest 1830, towgs84 +198,+881,+317) → WGS84. Required for L7014; a known PROJ pitfall (EPSG:3148 may drop towgs84).

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop (HITL)
nodes.detail: AI proposes → humans verify/correct/enrich → corrections retrain the model. Both a CV method and a community model. Inherited from NYPL Building Inspector + RapiD.

nodes.label: Geographical text analysis
nodes.detail: Geo-parsing + NER + relation extraction over historical corpora (Gregory). Applied to Annuaires de l’Indochine + colonial press, this populates VMA’s KG semi-automatically (SODUCO did this for Paris).

nodes.label: DL feature matching georef
nodes.detail: SIFT/SuperGlue-family transfer from known maps; RMSE <1% of diagonal on 83% of 86 Jerusalem maps. An automated-georef frontier — adjacent to, not covering, VMA’s series case.

nodes.label: OCR + geocoding georef
nodes.detail: Read place text on a map → geocode → derive control points (~316 m avg error). Cheap but coarse automated georef.

nodes.label: Procedural 3D / LoD2
nodes.detail: 2D footprints + probabilistic roof-type / height inference → procedural extrusion (Blender BCGA / GIS) → LoD2 CityJSON. No LiDAR needed. The histo3d back half.

nodes.label: Cross-edition transformer segmentation
nodes.detail: ETH IKG cross-attention spatio-temporal transformer that segments across multiple map editions → urban change detection over time, not just single-map vectorization.

nodes.label: Conzenian morphological analysis
nodes.detail: Decompose urban form into street system / plot pattern / building fabric → “plan units” marking growth phases. The vocabulary for VMA’s morphology reading.

nodes.label: Muratorian procedural typology
nodes.detail: Read the city as the organic result of building-type evolution. Conceptual base for procedural LoD2 modelling.

nodes.label: 6-layer world-as-data-stack
nodes.detail: The city as ascending layers L1 map raster → L2 3D → L3 road/facade → L4 fabric → L5 POI/economic → L6 memory. Dependency rule: layer N needs N-1. VMA’s build sequence.

nodes.label: Lefebvre’s triad
nodes.detail: Conçu (conceived: maps/plans → L1+L4), perçu (perceived: practice → L3+L5), vécu (lived: memory → L6). VMA maps the triad onto the data stack.

nodes.label: Body and soul
nodes.detail: Body = physical geometry (L1–L4); soul = sensory/social/economic/narrative meaning (L5–L6). The gap between them is what VMA exists to fill (after the Saigoneer framing).

nodes.label: digitized → digitalized → reconstructed
nodes.detail: Most archives stop at “digitized” (a scan exists). VMA targets “digitally reconstructed” (meaning + memory restored).

nodes.label: The production of space
nodes.detail: Lefebvre: space is socially produced, not a neutral container. The root claim under VMA’s whole interpretive frame.

nodes.label: The right to the city
nodes.detail: Lefebvre → Harvey: the claim of inhabitants to shape urbanization. Frames the “for whom was the city built?” question VMA poses of each regime.

nodes.label: Critical cartography
nodes.detail: Harley: maps are rhetoric + power, never neutral mirrors. The stance for reading colonial surveys as arguments, not facts.

nodes.label: Legibility / seeing like a state
nodes.detail: Scott: states simplify territory into maps + cadastres to make it governable. Explains why colonial Saigon was surveyed the way it was.

nodes.label: Spatial humanities
nodes.detail: Gregory’s deliberate expansion of HGIS-as-tool into a humanistic mode of argument. The disciplinary home for VMA’s method.

nodes.label: Historical GIS (HGIS)
nodes.detail: GIS with time as a first-class dimension: changing boundaries, shifting place names, uncertain sources. The technical genus VMA belongs to.

nodes.label: GAP: OBIA calibration for French colonial Indochina symbology
nodes.detail: Nobody has published a color/line/hatching calibration for Indochina maps. SODUCO (Paris), ETH (Swiss), Morlighem (Dutch) are adjacent, not this. VMA’s first publishable contribution.

nodes.label: GAP: automated georef of Indian-1960 military series
nodes.detail: No published GCP-propagation + Helmert-correction method for Indian-1960 datum series. DL feature-matching (Jerusalem) + OCR+geocode (Sanborn) are adjacent. The L7014 pipeline is novel.

nodes.label: GAP: geotemporal KG for a SE-Asian colonial city
nodes.detail: Amsterdam TM, Vienna Wiki, GLOBALISE exist for other regions; no street/building-level KG for any colonial Asian city. The Saigon 1880–1930 KG would be first.

nodes.label: GAP: spatial/GIS methods × colonial Saigon
nodes.detail: No published work combines GIS methods with French colonial Saigon. Closest analog: a Shanghai French Concession cadastral-GIS paper (Transactions in GIS, 2012) — the precursor VMA should cite.

nodes.label: Thongchai — Siam Mapped (1994)
nodes.detail: Geo-body theory: how mapping produced the modern Thai nation. Essential for critiquing SE-Asian colonial cartography. NOT in the library — acquire.

nodes.label: Anderson — Imagined Communities (1983)
nodes.detail: Census, map, and museum as the institutions of colonial nation-making. NOT in the library — acquire.

nodes.label: Cherry — Down and Out in Saigon (2019)
nodes.detail: The key recent social history of colonial Saigon. Cited but NOT in the library — acquire.

nodes.label: Brocheux & Hémery — Indochina (2009)
nodes.detail: The standard synthesis of Indochinese colonization 1858–1954. Cited but NOT in the library — acquire.

nodes.label: Mostern — The Yellow River (2021)
nodes.detail: Levenson-Prize monograph that grew out of World Historical Gazetteer infrastructure. The career-model output VMA aspires to. NOT in library.

nodes.label: Morlighem — histo3d thesis (2021)
nodes.detail: The reference end-to-end map→LoD2 pipeline + its strict-symbology caveat.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/04-vma-pipeline/Camille_Morlighem_p5_thesis Automatic reconstruction of 3D city models from historical maps.pdf

nodes.label: Annuaire général de l’Indochine
nodes.detail: Colonial trade directory (merchants, addresses, business types) — the primary corpus for VMA’s geographical-text-analysis → KG pipeline (the Annuaire is VMA’s equivalent of SODUCO’s Paris directories).

nodes.label: Huỳnh Thế Du — Quy hoạch Sài Gòn–TPHCM 1858–2024
nodes.detail: A planning-history synthesis of Saigon/HCMC across regimes — the Vietnamese-language backbone for the dissertation’s long arc.

source.ref: ~/Downloads/Urbanism/03-vietnam-indochina/Huynh The Du - Quy hoach Sai Gon - TPHCM 1858-2024 (2024).pdf

nodes.label: Bou Akar — For the War Yet to Come (2018)
nodes.detail: Decolonial post-conflict planning theory (Beirut). The supervisor framework VMA would apply to Saigon’s regime-layered arc.

nodes.label: Imago Mundi
nodes.detail: The only English-language journal devoted to the history of pre-modern maps. VMA’s venue for L7014 cartographic history + georef methodology.

nodes.label: Planning Perspectives
nodes.detail: Urban-planning history; explicitly covers colonial urbanism. The venue for the OBIA paper framed as planning history (and Njoh’s home journal).

nodes.label: Int. J. of Geographical Information Science
nodes.detail: Methods venue for the OBIA-calibration contribution.

nodes.label: ISPRS Annals
nodes.detail: Photogrammetry/remote-sensing venue for the georef-propagation pipeline.

nodes.label: CHR (Computational Humanities Research)
nodes.detail: Receptive to tool/pipeline papers; target for the L7014 + KG methods.

nodes.label: DH (ADHO Annual)
nodes.detail: The DH flagship conference; Spatial Humanities SIG. 2026 South Korea suits SE-Asian work.

nodes.label: Spatial Humanities (conference)
nodes.detail: Biennial; both Gregory + McDonough present here. The most directly relevant venue for VMA’s first paper.

nodes.label: Digital Scholarship in the Humanities
nodes.detail: European DH flagship journal; target for the geographical-text-analysis → KG paper.

nodes.label: Journal of Vietnamese Studies
nodes.detail: Premier English-language Vietnamese-studies venue; the home for VMA’s humanistic Saigon results.

nodes.label: Journal of Southeast Asian Studies
nodes.detail: Flagship regional journal; comparative colonial history.

nodes.label: Urban History
nodes.detail: Cambridge; international interdisciplinary urban-history flagship — target for the spatial-history-of-Saigon paper.

nodes.label: Digital Humanities Quarterly
nodes.detail: Open-access DH field journal.

nodes.label: Pica Foundation
nodes.detail: Funds Allmaps — the infrastructure VMA depends on.

nodes.label: NEH Office of Digital Humanities
nodes.detail: DH Advancement Grant (Exploration ~$50K): lowest-barrier funder for tools + data infrastructure; US-applicant advantage.

nodes.label: Mellon Foundation
nodes.detail: Digital Humanities Asia (Stanford Sawyer Seminar precedent) — highest relevance to SE-Asia specifically.

nodes.label: ANR (France)
nodes.detail: Funded SODUCO; requires a French academic co-PI — unlockable via EFEO / Sciences Po.

nodes.label: Horizon Europe
nodes.detail: European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage; needs an EU consortium — a TU Delft partnership opens it. Funded Time Machine Europe.

nodes.label: Henry Luce Foundation
nodes.detail: Funds Fulbright’s Digitizing Việt Nam (textual). Regional-heritage funder worth monitoring.
